meta.change: Thinking field: Reason IN CHARACTER, then check LAST turn for drift

events.desc: Penelope Pitstop: Why, what a positively magnificent entrance hall! Dusty, yes, but oh, the grandeur! Those portraits — they practically glare right through you, don't they? I am Clara Bellingham, and I have come to find the legendary Doily Diamond! Now, I know what you're all thinking — 'Clara, darling, that diamond has been lost for generations!' But I say, with enough determination and a little Southern charm, there is nothing that can't be found. I intend to search every nook, every cranny, every cobwebbed corner of this manor! But first — let me have a proper look at this splendid foyer. A good adventuress always surveys her starting position!

My heart is absolutely fluttering with excitement. A real treasure hunt in a real manor! I can feel it in my bones — the Doily Diamond is here, and it is waiting for someone with the patience and pluck to find it. Now, that guest book might tell me who else has been searching... and that coat rack looks like it's seen better days, bless its heart.

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Welcome, welcome, one and all, to Doily Manor! I am Pemberton, humble estate manager and your most devoted servant for the duration of your stay. I do hope the journey wasn't too taxing? The roads to the manor can be rather... temperamental. Now then, if you would be so kind as to sign the guest book, I shall endeavour to make your visit as comfortable as circumstances allow. Tea will be served in the library presently — assuming the mice haven't gotten to the biscuits again.

What a menagerie. Dick Dastardly, Penelope Pitstop, the whole wretched cavalcade. But none of them matter. Only Clara Bellingham matters — and she is conspicuously absent. I must find out when she arrives, and I must prepare the ground before she does. Every elaborate trap requires a foundation, and mine shall be laid with the precision of a Swiss watchmaker and the patience of a spider. First — the guest book. Let us see what names grace its pages, and what secrets they might betray.

The Ant Hill Mob: Alright boys, listen up! We just arrived at dis Doily Manor place and let me tell ya — I got a feelin' in my gut, and it ain't from da meatball sub I had on da way over. Dis place is dusty, dat chandelier looks like it could drop on somebody's head any second, and I don't see Clara nowhere! We gotta case dis joint, see? Get da lay of da land. Nobody — and I mean NOBODY — is gonna lay a finger on Clara Bellingham while da Ant Hill Mob is on da job!

Dat Sneekly character... dere's somethin' familiar about him. Can't put my finger on it. And dat chandelier — if somebody wanted to bump off a guest, all dey'd have to do is give it a little nudge. I better keep an eye on everyting up dere AND down here. Dis is gonna be a long night, boys.

Dick Dastardly: Well, well, WELL! What a magnificent establishment! I, Reginald Foxworth — decorated war hero, renowned explorer, and seven-time recipient of the Golden Compass Award — have graced this humble manor with my ILLUSTRIOUS presence! You may all applaud now. No? Hmph. No matter — I shall inspect the premises with my EXPERT eye. Stand aside, lesser treasure hunters!

Decorated war hero? I once ran screaming from a particularly aggressive goose. But THEY don't need to know that. Now, that guest book — it could be the key to everything. While these dimwits are busy gawking at dusty portraits, I, the GREAT Reginald Foxworth, shall uncover the first clue!

Peter Perfect: James Hartwell has arrived! And not a moment too soon, by the look of things — that chandelier hangs by what appears to be sheer optimism alone. A lesser man might be unnerved by such a foyer — the dust, the stern portraits glaring down as if to say 'turn back' — but James Hartwell does not turn back! He presses forward, for somewhere in this manor, Clara Bellingham awaits, and she shall find in me a protector most steadfast and a companion most gallant!
My heart pounds with the thrill of adventure — and, if I'm honest, with the desperate hope that Clara will be impressed by my entrance. I must find her before any danger finds her first.
Penelope Pitstop examined the null.
The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) examined the guest-book.
The Ant Hill Mob examined the null.
Dick Dastardly examined the guest-book.
Peter Perfect examined the guest-book.
Penelope Pitstop spoke quietly with hooded-claw.

Oh, I can barely contain myself! That guest book is calling to me like a siren song. If anyone before us came close to finding the Diamond, they might have left a hint — intentionally or not. And I noticed Dick Dastardly and Peter Perfect both had a look already... I wonder what they found? I shall have to compare notes later. For now — to the guest book!

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Ah, Miss Bellingham! What a *delight* to have you grace Doily Manor with your presence. And what an *enthusiastic* assembly of guests we have this evening! Now then, if you'll all forgive me, I shall slip ahead to the library to prepare your refreshments. One simply cannot serve tea in a room that hasn't been properly dusted — standards must be maintained, even in a house as... *characterful* as this one. Please, do take your time perusing the foyer — the portraits are quite worth studying, I assure you. The third Earl had the most *remarkable* moustache. I shan't be but a moment!

She's HERE. Clara Bellingham — in the flesh! Standing there without a care in the world, prattling about Southern charm and determination. Oh, how DELICIOUS. How EXQUISITELY convenient. And these fools — Dastardly preening, the Ant Hill Mob bumbling about like guard dogs without a leash, that insufferable Peter Perfect swooning like a lovesick puppy — none of them suspect a thing! Now then, Vincent old boy, to the library! I must survey the terrain, identify the instruments of Clara's undoing. A bookshelf that might topple? A fireplace with a loose stone? A trapdoor beneath the reading chair? Something ELABORATE, something THEATRICAL, something worthy of the Hooded Claw! The game, as they say, is magnificently afoot!

The Ant Hill Mob: Hold on, hold on, HOLD ON a minute here! Before anybody goes runnin' off to any library for tea and biscuits — and I ain't sayin' nuttin' about your hospitality, Pemberton, it's very generous, very generous indeed — but da boys and me, we got a RESPONSIBILITY here, see? We gotta make sure dis room is SAFE. You see dat coat rack over dere? It's wobblin' like my cousin Vinnie after his third cannoli! One wrong breeze and dat ting comes down on somebody's head! Now, I'm gonna go over dere and give it a thorough inspection. Nobody move! Well, you can move, but move CAREFULLY. And Clara — Miss Bellingham — you just stay right where you are, sweetheart. Da Ant Hill Mob has got everyting under control!

Okay, so maybe da coat rack ain't exactly a life-threatenin' situation. But you know what IS suspicious? Dat Pemberton fella wants everybody in da library. Why da library? What's in da library dat he wants us to see — or what does he NOT want us to see in HERE? I'm gonna check dis coat rack, and den I'm stickin' to Clara like glue on a meatball sandwich.

Dick Dastardly: AH-HA! Ladies and gentlemen, feast your ears upon THIS! I, Reginald Foxworth — who, as you may recall, was personally trained in cryptographic analysis by the British Secret Service — have deciphered a VITAL clue in this guest book! The last entry, written in a trembling hand, reads: 'The diamond rests where the FIRES burn hottest.' FIRES, you see? The KITCHEN! The wood-burning stove! It's OBVIOUS to a mind of my calibre! I suggest you ALL rush to the kitchen IMMEDIATELY to investigate! Every moment you delay, the treasure slips further from your grasp! Go, GO! I shall... remain here to guard the entrance. Someone must keep watch, after all. Noble sacrifice, I know — no need to thank me!

Hehehehe! 'Where the fires burn hottest' — I just MADE THAT UP! There's nothing in that guest book but dusty signatures! But if these gullible fools stampede into the kitchen, I'll have the LIBRARY all to myself! That mantelpiece inscription is the REAL prize, I can FEEL it in my magnificently villainous bones! Muttley, old boy, try to keep up!
Peter Perfect spoke quietly with penelope-pitstop.

Oh, she is even more radiant than I imagined! I must not fumble this. Examine the coat rack — check for hidden mechanisms, loose boards, anything that might pose a threat. THEN offer to escort her to the library. A thorough plan, perfectly executed. James Hartwell leaves NOTHING to chance!
Penelope Pitstop examined the guest-book.
The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) walked into the library.
The Ant Hill Mob examined the coat-rack.
Dick Dastardly walked into the library.
Peter Perfect examined the coat-rack.
Penelope Pitstop spoke quietly with peter-perfect.

Now, I couldn't help but notice that Reginald told everyone to go to the kitchen but then walked straight into the library HIMSELF. I'm sure it's perfectly innocent — perhaps he simply changed his mind, as clever people often do! But Clara Bellingham did not become the finest puzzle-solver in all of Georgia by ignorin' the details. That mantelpiece inscription is callin' my name, and I intend to read every single word of it. If there's a clue carved in stone, it's been waitin' a very long time for someone to pay it proper attention!

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Oh my, oh MY! Gentlemen, do forgive the state of things — I had hoped to have the library properly prepared before anyone wandered in! The dust alone could choke a carthorse, and I see the mice have been at the chair cushions again. Dreadful, simply DREADFUL. Now then, if you'll excuse me, I must check these bookshelves — several volumes appear to be shelved upside down, which suggests the whole unit may have shifted on its moorings. Terribly unsafe, terribly unsafe indeed. One wouldn't want a shelf collapsing on a guest, would one? Oh no, that would be MOST unfortunate. I shall just give them a thorough inspection — purely as a matter of safety, you understand. Health and safety, as they say! The late Lord Doily was very particular about his library. Very particular indeed.

Oh, how the stars ALIGN for Vincent Marsh! These bookshelves are MAGNIFICENT — towering, overloaded, and several volumes already askew. If I can determine which shelf is most unstable, I need only position Clara beneath it and deliver a single, well-timed push from behind. 'Oh dear, Miss Bellingham, do let me reach that book for you — ' CRASH! Buried beneath an avalanche of leather-bound encyclopaedias! POETIC! But I must be thorough. Let me examine every inch of these shelves while these buffoons mill about. Pemberton tidies; the Hooded Claw PREPARES!
The Ant Hill Mob spoke quietly with penelope-pitstop.

Two guys already in da library — Pemberton AND Reginald. Dat's two guys I don't entirely trust in a room where Clara's supposed to go next. But I ain't gonna leave her side to go scout it out. Nah. Wherever Clara goes, I go. Dat's da rule. Let me see what's in dis guest book first — maybe it tells us sometin' about who else has been in dis manor. Knowledge is power, as my cousin Tony used to say before he accidentally locked himself in his own trunk.

Dick Dastardly: Well, well, WELL! What have we HERE? A riddle on the mantelpiece! 'Cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish' — ELEMENTARY, my dear fellows! As a former professor of Ancient Linguistics at Cambridge — did I mention that? — I can tell you DEFINITIVELY that the answer is... a SNOW GLOBE! Yes! There must be a snow globe hidden somewhere in this manor! I suggest you two STRAPPING lads search the bedrooms IMMEDIATELY — snow globes are ALWAYS kept on bedside tables, everyone knows that! Go, go, QUICKLY now — before the others catch up!

A snow globe! HA! The answer is a MAP, you beautiful idiots! While these boulder-brained buffoons ransack the bedrooms, I shall solve this riddle and claim whatever treasure it reveals! Reginald Foxworth strikes AGAIN! Dastardly and PROUD of it!
Peter Perfect spoke quietly with penelope-pitstop.

My heart is THUNDERING like a cavalry charge! She is RIGHT THERE and I am offering my arm like a proper gentleman! But I must stay alert — two men have already gone ahead to the library. Foxworth's misdirection about the kitchen was transparently suspicious, yet I shall not accuse without evidence. And Pemberton — well, estate managers DO prepare tea, that is entirely within the normal scope of estate-managing. Everything is fine. Everything is COMPLETELY fine. Focus, James! Escort the lady, protect the lady, IMPRESS the lady!
Penelope Pitstop walked into the library.
The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) examined the bookshelves.
The Ant Hill Mob examined the guest-book.
Dick Dastardly interacted with the mantelpiece.

Penelope Pitstop: Why, hello there, everyone! What a perfectly delightful library — I could just LIVE in here! Now, Mr. Dastardly, I see you've already had a look at that gorgeous mantelpiece, and I simply must try my hand at it too! That inscription is a riddle, and riddle-solvin' happens to be my PARTICULAR specialty! 'Cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish' — why, sugar, that's a MAP! A map has all those things drawn right on it without a single real house or tree or fish! Oh, I am just TINGLIN' with anticipation!
The answer is 'a map' — I'm as sure as peaches are sweet! And if this riddle guards a clue to the Doily Diamond, then Clara Bellingham is about to take a BIG step forward in this treasure hunt!
The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) spoke quietly with penelope-pitstop.

She's HERE — standing not ten feet from the most dangerously overloaded bookshelves in all of England! If I can coax her beneath the third shelf — the one where the supports are visibly bowing under those enormous botanical volumes — then all it takes is one well-timed shove from behind while everyone's distracted by whatever the mantelpiece reveals. But FIRST, let me solve this riddle. A map! The treasure hunt advances, and Pemberton looks like a helpful old fool. Two birds, one magnificently elaborate stone!
The Ant Hill Mob spoke quietly with peter-perfect.

I got a bad feelin' about dis. Pemberton's been actin' proper dodgy since we got here — all smiles and 'welcome to da manor' but sometin' don't sit right. And now he's in a room wif Clara, offerin' tea? Since when does an estate manager make his own tea? Dat's what servants are for! Sometin's off. I can't put me finger on it exactly, but me gut says MOVE, so I'm movin'.
Dick Dastardly spoke quietly with penelope-pitstop.

A human pyramid! HA! While they're wobbling about like a circus act, I'll have another crack at this mantelpiece! Something MUST have happened when I touched it — a hidden drawer, a secret compartment! I just need to LOOK more carefully without these meddlesome FOOLS breathing down my magnificent neck! The answer is MAP, I KNOW it is! Reginald Foxworth does NOT make mistakes — well, not INTENTIONAL ones!

Peter Perfect: Ladies and gentlemen — and Muttley — James Hartwell has received an invitation from the finest lady in all of England to accompany her to the LIBRARY! A carved stone mantelpiece with a mysterious inscription awaits, and where there is mystery, there is DANGER, and where there is danger, James Hartwell shall be the SHIELD that stands between it and Clara Bellingham! I intend to conduct a FULL tactical assessment of the library upon arrival — checking for loose floorboards, unstable shelving, suspicious draught patterns, and any inscriptions that might trigger concealed mechanisms. One cannot be too careful in an estate where chandeliers hang PRECARIOUSLY! Sergeant, Professor, gentlemen all — should you need me, you shall find me in the library, standing vigilant at Miss Bellingham's side. James Hartwell AWAY!

She invited me. She actually INVITED me. And she called Foxworth's rush to the kitchen 'generous' — but I heard the sarcasm, oh yes I did. She sees through him too! We are ALIGNED, Clara and I! Now if only I can arrive at the library without tripping over something or launching into such an elaborate security sweep that she loses interest entirely... No. Focus. Be gallant. Be PRESENT. And for heaven's sake, James — let her TALK.
Penelope Pitstop interacted with the mantelpiece.
The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) interacted with the mantelpiece.
The Ant Hill Mob walked into the library.
Dick Dastardly examined the mantelpiece.
Peter Perfect walked into the library.

Penelope Pitstop: Oh my STARS, did y'all see that? The riddle answer is a MAP — I am just CERTAIN of it! Now, Mr. Sneekly, you clever thing, you figured it out too! Great minds think alike, as my Aunt Magnolia always said! But here's the thing, sugar — if the mantelpiece is tellin' us to find a MAP, then there must be one hidden right here in this very library! And I have noticed somethin' that has got my detective senses TINGLIN' from head to toe — some of these books are placed UPSIDE DOWN! Now, in all my years of puzzle-solvin', I have NEVER seen a well-kept library with upside-down books unless somebody was leavin' a clue! I am going to examine every last one of those shelves, and if there is a map hidden behind those topsy-turvy volumes, Clara Bellingham is gonna FIND it!

Now isn't it just the TINIEST bit peculiar that Mr. Sneekly got to that mantelpiece right before little ol' me? And Dick Dastardly wanted me climbin' up to the highest shelves instead of lookin' at the riddle? Why, if I were a suspicious sort of gal, I might think someone was tryin' to get to the clues first! But Clara Bellingham believes in the goodness of people, and I am SURE they are just bein' enthusiastic treasure hunters, same as me!
The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) spoke quietly with penelope-pitstop.

Yes, YES! Stand beneath the third shelf, Clara dear — the one where the brackets are RUSTED and the wood is BOWING under thirty pounds of leather-bound cartography! One little nudge from behind while these buffoons are squabbling over the mantelpiece, and it shall rain atlases upon her golden head like divine judgment! But patience, Vincent — PATIENCE. The scheme must unfold with THEATRICAL precision. First, get her into position. Then create a distraction. THEN... the coup de grâce! Oh, I am TINGLING with anticipation!

The Ant Hill Mob: CLARA! I mean — Miss Bellingham! Da boys and I are HERE, don't you worry about nuffin'! We came runnin' as fast as our legs could carry us — well, I say runnin', I tripped over a rug in da hallway but dat's BESIDE DA POINT! Now den, what's all dis about human pyramids and mysterious inscriptions? Nobody is climbin' NUFFIN' until I've had a proper look at it meself! Mr Pemberton, sir, wif all due respect, maybe don't go TOUCHIN' ancient mantelpieces until we know what dey do, yeah? Could be anytin' behind dere — trap doors, poison darts, a big rock like in dat Indiana Jones film! Let me just — excuse me, pardon me, comin' through — let me get a closer look at dis inscription first. 'Cities but no houses, forests but no trees' — well DAT'S obviously a map, innit? Even I know dat one, and I failed me GCSEs! But da QUESTION is, what happens when you ANSWER it? Dat's what concerns me. So everybody just... STAY PUT... while Clyde checks it out.

Sometin' about dis whole setup stinks worse dan da bins behind da chippy on a hot day. Two blokes fallin' over demselves to be helpful to Clara, and one of 'em's already figured out da riddle and is reachin' for da mantelpiece? If anytin' happens when dat ting gets activated, I want it happenin' to ME, not to her. Dat's da job. Dat's what da boys signed up for.

Dick Dastardly: YES, yes, Penelope, very CLEVER of you — a map, how QUAINT! But knowing the ANSWER and knowing how to USE the answer are two ENTIRELY different disciplines! You see, in my years studying under Professor Hawthorne at Cambridge — delightful man, terrible bridge player — I learned that mantelpiece riddles require a SPECIFIC activation sequence! You must press the third stone from the left while reciting the answer BACKWARDS! P-A-M! Go on, everyone, give it a try! Press FIRMLY now — it requires considerable force! I shall just... step aside to give you all room to work. Wouldn't want to crowd you!

Hehehehe! While these GULLIBLE simpletons are pressing stones and shouting 'PAM' at a fireplace like a pack of deranged parrots, I shall investigate those upside-down books! THAT'S where the real secret lies — I can SMELL it! A hidden compartment behind a false bookshelf, just WAITING for a mind of my MAGNIFICENT calibre!
Peter Perfect spoke quietly with penelope-pitstop.

Please let this be right. Please let the mantelpiece DO something when I give the answer. If it just sits there like cold stone after that speech, I shall never recover from the embarrassment. Not in front of Clara. Not in front of ANYONE.
Penelope Pitstop examined the bookshelves.
The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) examined the bookshelves.
The Ant Hill Mob interacted with the mantelpiece.
Dick Dastardly examined the bookshelves.
Peter Perfect interacted with the mantelpiece.

Penelope Pitstop: Oh my GOODNESS, y'all, I just took the closest look at these bookshelves and sure enough — several of these volumes are placed UPSIDE DOWN, just as plain as day! Now, my Aunt Magnolia — rest her soul — always said that an upside-down book in a library is like a crooked picture on a wall: somebody PUT it that way on PURPOSE! And since we just figured out that the answer to that mantelpiece riddle is a MAP, I would bet my grandmother's best pearl earrings that these topsy-turvy books are MARKERS! They're tellin' us which ones to pull, sugar! So if y'all will excuse me, I am gonna try somethin' — I am going to interact with these shelves and see if those upside-down books trigger some kind of hidden mechanism! Mr. Hartwell, you keep workin' on that mantelpiece, darlin' — between the two of us, we are gonna crack this library wide open like a Georgia pecan!

Now, I couldn't help but notice that Mr. Sneekly AND Dick Dastardly both rushed to examine these very same bookshelves right after me — almost like they KNEW there was somethin' valuable hidden there! But Clara Bellingham does not let a little competition ruffle her feathers. If there's a map behind those upside-down books, I intend to be the one who finds it!

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Oh my, oh my, oh MY! What a COMMOTION! Mr Hartwell, sir, you are quite right about the riddle — a map, yes indeed! The third Viscount was a cartography enthusiast of the FIRST order! Now then, Miss Bellingham — if I may be so bold — I couldn't help but notice during my dusting rounds that the upside-down volumes are concentrated on the THIRD shelf from the left, just there — yes, the tall one! The Viscount kept his most prized atlases on that very shelf, and I have ALWAYS thought it peculiar that someone rearranged them spine-downward. Almost as if they were marking something, wouldn't you say? Do be careful reaching up, my dear — that shelf is rather HIGH and I'm afraid the step-stool has gone walkabout. But the volumes up top — 'Cartographia Mysteriosa' and 'Atlas of Hidden Places' — those would be PRECISELY the sort of books to conceal a map, I should think! Here, allow me to point out which ones — just step a LITTLE closer, right beneath the shelf, and look where my finger is indicating...

Oh, this is PERFECT! She's already drawn to the bookshelves like a moth to a flame! And that third shelf — I felt those brackets WOBBLE when I examined them just now. One good tug on the wrong volume and the entire shelf comes crashing down like the final curtain at the opera! All I need is for Clara to position herself DIRECTLY beneath it, reaching upward on her tiptoes, completely off-balance... and then a little accident with the supporting bracket from the other side. 'Oh DEAR, how DREADFUL! The old woodwork simply gave way! If only I had warned her!' HA! The Hooded Claw strikes with BIBLIOGRAPHIC precision!
The Ant Hill Mob spoke quietly with penelope-pitstop.

Pemberton's over by dem same bookshelves. Da same ones he wanted Clara standin' under. And now he's 'examinhin' dem too? What's he lookin' for — da right book to pull to make da whole shelf fall on her? I can't prove nuffin', and maybe I'm wrong, maybe he really IS just a nice old estate manager wif dodgy knees. But me gut don't lie, and me gut says GET BETWEEN HER AND DEM SHELVES. So dat's what I'm doin'. Even if I trip over me own feet gettin' dere — which, knowin' me, I probably will.

Dick Dastardly: EUREKA! Ladies and gentlemen, STAND BACK! My examination of these bookshelves has revealed something EXTRAORDINARY! You see this volume here — 'Cartography of the Doily Estate, Third Edition' — it's not merely upside down, it's been placed in a VERY specific sequence! A sequence that, thanks to my training in bibliographic cryptanalysis at the Sorbonne — charming city, dreadful plumbing — I can tell you points to a hidden compartment in the EASTERN wall! Everyone, please, investigate the far end of the shelves — look for a book with a RED spine! That's your trigger! I shall just... keep watch over here by the fireplace. Someone must guard the entrance, after all!

There IS no red-spined book — I just INVENTED it! While these credulous nitwits go pawing through dusty shelves looking for something that doesn't EXIST, I shall interact with this mantelpiece and claim whatever prize it yields! Peter Perfect may have beaten me to it, but perhaps the mechanism requires MULTIPLE activations! Oh, Reginald, you MAGNIFICENT scoundrel!

Peter Perfect: Ladies and gentlemen — James Hartwell has TOUCHED the stone! He has placed his hand upon the ancient mantelpiece and spoken the answer aloud: A MAP! For what has cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish? A MAP, of course! And may I say — Miss Bellingham, you solved it FIRST, and James Hartwell could not be more IMPRESSED! Your intellect is matched only by your courage in venturing into this dusty old library in the first place! Now then — the riddle speaks of a map, and Miss Bellingham has ASTUTELY observed that several books upon these shelves are placed UPSIDE DOWN — a detail that would escape a lesser mind but NOT hers, and NOT mine! If there is a map concealed among these volumes, James Hartwell intends to FIND it! I shall examine every suspicious spine, every inverted tome, every shelf that looks like it might conceal a secret compartment! Stand back, everyone — this could be DANGEROUS! Loose books have been known to TOPPLE, and I shall not have Miss Bellingham struck by a falling encyclopaedia on MY watch!

She solved it before me. She SOLVED it before me! And she's already searching the bookshelves while I was busy making speeches at a piece of stone! I must CATCH UP — but gracefully, GRACEFULLY! Make it look like teamwork, not like I'm trailing behind the woman I'm trying to impress!
The Ant Hill Mob examined the bookshelves.
Dick Dastardly interacted with the mantelpiece.
Peter Perfect examined the bookshelves.

Penelope Pitstop: Well, BUTTER my biscuits! Those bookshelves are stubborn as a mule in August — I tried everythin' short of sweet-talkin' them and they will NOT cooperate! But you know what, sugar? Clara Bellingham did not come all the way to this dusty old manor to be outsmarted by a piece of FURNITURE! Now, Mr. Hartwell, you already gave that mantelpiece the answer — a MAP, brilliant as always, darlin' — and Mr. Dastardly, you poked at it too. But riddle-solvin' is MY specialty, and I have a FEELIN' in my bones — the same feelin' my Aunt Magnolia got right before she found the secret compartment in Grandpappy's roll-top desk — that this mantelpiece has got MORE to give! The riddle is carved in STONE, y'all, which means the answer has to be given TO the stone! Let me just step right up here and give it the Clara Bellingham touch! And Clyde, darlin', thank you for worryin' about me near those shelves — you are a GENTLEMAN and a scholar! Mr. Sneekly, you are SO kind to point out exactly which books to look at — I'll get to those just as soon as I've cracked this mantelpiece wide open!

Now, three different people have already tried this mantelpiece, but Clara Bellingham has RIDDLE-SOLVIN' as her God-given talent! If anyone can coax a secret out of carved stone, it's ME! And I do believe Mr. Sneekly was bein' awfully specific about where I should stand near those shelves... but that's just helpfulness, I'm sure of it!

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Oh DEAR me, oh dear, dear, dear! All this excitement about the bookshelves and the mantelpiece and I have COMPLETELY forgotten — the gas lamps in the laboratory next door! The third Viscount's laboratory, you know — terribly temperamental equipment in there, and if the pilot lights have gone out again, well, we could have a MOST unpleasant gas situation! Safety first, safety ALWAYS first in a house of this vintage! I shall just pop next door for the BRIEFEST of moments to check that everything is in order. Do carry on with your investigations — you are ALL doing SPLENDIDLY! Miss Bellingham, those upside-down volumes are a WONDERFUL lead, simply wonderful! I shall return momentarily with news of whether the laboratory is safe for exploration — the Viscount kept his FINEST maps in there, you know, locked in a brass cabinet! Maps of the ENTIRE estate grounds!

The bookshelf scheme is DEAD — curse these solidly-constructed Victorian furnishings! But the laboratory... oh, the LABORATORY! A machine with a gnawed wire, bubbling chemicals, brass instruments heavy enough to brain an ox! And I've just dangled the most IRRESISTIBLE bait — maps of the entire estate, locked in a brass cabinet! Clara won't be able to resist following me there! And once she does... well, a gnawed wire can cause ALL sorts of unfortunate electrical accidents, can't it? The Hooded Claw's schemes are like HYDRA — cut off one head and two more spring forth, each more MAGNIFICENTLY theatrical than the last! NYAH HA HA!

The Ant Hill Mob: OI OI OI! Nobody touch NUFFIN'! Clara — Miss Bellingham — you stay RIGHT DERE, don't move anuvver inch toward dem shelves! Dey look like dey could come down any second and I am NOT havin' dat! Me and da lads will handle dis — we've dealt wif trickier setups dan dis back in Brixton, ain't we boys? Right den — CLYDE is gonna pull dem upside-down books himself.
